item.title: Sri Lanka rout Pakistan by 8 wickets to eliminate England from ODI tri-series final
item.description: Sri Lanka delivered a commanding eight-wicket victory over Pakistan on Tuesday, producing a clinical all-round performance to knock England out of contention for the ODI tri-series final. Fast bowler Dilshan Madushanka led the charge with a career-best five-wicket haul before Kamindu Mendis anchored a comfortable chase, giving Sri Lanka a timely boost ahead of the title clash. Madushanka's career-best five-for dismantles Pakistan Madushanka returned figures of 5-34 as Pakistan were bowled out for just 110 after Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis won the toss and elected to field at the Gaddafi Stadium. Pakistan, who had already secured their place in the final, struggled to cope with Madushanka's bowling as Sri Lanka's attack dismantled their batting line-up. The hosts were unable to build a substantial partnership, leaving Sri Lanka with a modest target to chase. Kamindu Mendis anchors comfortable chase In reply, Sri Lanka raced to 114-2 in just 18.1 overs, completing the chase well before the floodlight towers were fully switched on for the day-night encounter. Kamindu starred with an unbeaten 62 off 60 deliveries, striking eight fours and two sixes. He survived an early reprieve after being dropped by the wicketkeeper before opening his account and later overturned an on-field lbw decision on 44 after successfully reviewing the call. The left-hander brought up his half-century in memorable fashion, pulling a delivery for six after substitute fielder Ghazi Ghori had touched the boundary with his foot while completing a catch. Sri Lanka bounce back as England crash out Sri Lanka's emphatic win came after their remarkable chase of 430 against England in Rawalpindi, the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. The latest result also served as a strong response to their 37-run defeat against Pakistan in the tournament opener. Pakistan had already secured their place in the final after winning their first two matches against England, including a thrilling one-wicket victory on Sunday. They finished the league stage with six points from three wins. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, have four points and will face England on Thursday in their final league fixture as they prepare for Saturday's final against Pakistan. England's hopes of reaching the title clash ended with Sri Lanka's dominant performance.

item.title: Browns have apparently made their final Shedeur Sanders trade decision
item.description: Browns have apparently made their final Shedeur Sanders trade decision originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns have a lot of quarterbacks on their hands, especially after activating Dillon Gabriel. But as the trade deadline of Nov. 10 nears, there's one quarterback who's getting a lot of attention: Shedeur Sanders. Will the Browns trade him and get something in return? The Browns got people questioning the futures of both Sanders and Gabriel after they officially activated Gabriel off injured reserve this week. Now, the team has Sanders and Gabriel, as well as starting quarterback Deshaun Watson and rookie Taylen Green on its roster. That's a lot of signal-callers. Having all those guys has made some question if Sanders is on the trading block. Cleveland Browns insider reveals Shedeur Sanders' trade status ahead of NFL trade deadline According to a Browns insider, Sanders isn't on that trading block. At least not for this season. Per Browns reporter Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer , Sanders and Gabriel are both going to stay with the team through the NFL trade deadline. She also says that Sanders is still QB2 for the team's upcoming game against the Pittsburgh Steelers , even with Gabriel getting activated before Week 8. "To make room for Gabriel, the Browns waived seventh-round tight end Carsen Ryan, but will likely re-sign him to the practice squad if he clears waivers," Cabot stated in a piece. "The Browns always preferred to keep all four quarterbacks on the roster, and found a way to do it. If they had to move one of them, they would've tried to get Green through waivers and onto the practice squad, but it would've been risky." So, Sanders is here to stay, for now. The Browns' next game against the Steelers is an important one, since both are at the top of the AFC North and both have 5-2 records . item.title: Bengals urged not to make an RB trade despite Chase Brown's struggles
item.description: Bengals urged not to make an RB trade despite Chase Brown's struggles originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cincinnati Bengals are 4-2 heading into the team's Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans , as they are coming off a blowout win over the Baltimore Ravens . In the win, running back Chase Brown once again had an underwhelming day. With his struggles and the potential of RBs Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley available for trade, a blockbuster RB trade would seem possible. However, ESPN's Dan Graziano is urging the Bengals not to make a trade for an RB, and instead give Brown more time as the lead back this season, looking for upgrades elsewhere on the roster. Bengals urged not to add to RB room despite Chase Brown's struggles "If I were the Bengals, I'd be looking harder at potentially available linebackers or defensive backs ahead of the trade deadline than running backs," Graziano writes. The Bengals are likely trade deadline buyers this season, but adding someone like Taylor or Barkley wouldn't make much sense. While the appeal of adding either player is there, the price tag on both, financially and trade compensation-wise, should make a trade a lot less appealing to the Bengals than to some other teams. MORE : NFL insiders reveal four landing spots for Colts ’ Jonathan Taylor Besides, even though Brown is struggling this year, he started slow last season, and turned things around down the stretch, finishing with 1,019 rushing yards and six touchdowns last season for Cincinnati. Graziano believes "it would be very unlike Cincinnati to surrender draft capital for them." As good as Taylor and Barkley would be on this Bengals offense, it just doesn't make sense to swing such a trade. Instead, Graziano believes the Bengals should look to upgrade their linebacker and defensive back room. And if they want to upgrade the offense, eyeing an offensive lineman or a tight end would make a lot more sense. item.title: Lancs treatment of Anderson 'disrespectful' - Broad
item.description: Stuart Broad (left) and James Anderson (right) led England's bowling attack together for a generation until the former retired at the end of the 2023 Ashes [Getty Images] Lancashire have been "pretty disrespectful" in their treatment of legendary bowler James Anderson, says his long-time England bowler partner Stuart Broad. Anderson, 44, was told last week he will not have his contract renewed by the Red Rose county, ending his 26-year professional career with the club. Anderson took 50 wickets in the County Championship last season and served as captain, but incoming director of cricket Paul Farbrace has decided he wants to rebuild the struggling side, who finished second bottom in Division Two of the County Championship, for the future without England's all-time leading wicket-taker. "I didn't like it from Lancashire," Broad said on the For The Love of Cricket podcast . "It was not done in the right way. I think it was disrespectful. "You give your icons or greats of the game a better send off than that." Is this the end for Jimmy Anderson? Lancashire consider Anderson farewell amid fan unrest Farbrace, who moved from Sussex at the end of the season, has not yet officially started in his new role at Lancashire but delivered the news to Anderson at a meeting last week alongside chief executive Richard Kenyon, who has also recently been appointed. The news was first reported on Wednesday and Lancashire did not comment officially until Sunday. At a meeting with members on Monday, the club said they would look into arranging Anderson a farewell . "It shows a lack of leadership at that club," said Broad, whose combined total of Test wickets with Anderson stands at a record 1,039 in 138 Tests. "It shows a lack of doing it the right way. "Paul Farbrace is new, but where is the chair? Where is the board demanding that this is done in a better way?" Speaking publicly for the first time since the decision on Sunday, Anderson, who also had his England career cut short in 2024 in similar circumstances , expressed his sadness at the situation but stopped short of retiring. Other counties are understood to be interested in signing the veteran. "I get the thought process, 'we could probably get two half-decent cricketers for the one and losing that salary'," Broad added. "It doesn't surprise me that some counties have already been on the phone and seeing what his interest levels are. "I don't know what his next steps are. I think his statement was quite interesting. "There will be a lot of counties that want him. He offers a huge amount, he's still one of the best bowlers in the country." item.title: Cowboys’ win over Eagles has not changed Troy Aikman’s opinion about Dallas
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys earned an important 38-21 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football. However, former Cowboys quarterback Troy Aikman remains cautious about the NFL team’s playoff chances despite the impressive result. Speaking on ESPN’s Monday Night Football, Aikman explained why the victory had not significantly changed his assessment of Dallas. The Cowboys improved to 3-4, ending their two-game losing skid with a strong performance at Lincoln Financial Field. When Scott Van Pelt asked whether the win changed his outlook for Dallas’ upcoming schedule, Aikman delivered a measured response. “Not really. I mean, not really, and I don’t mean that as a negative,” Aikman said. “This is a beat-up Philadelphia team. I mean, come in here and win tonight. I mean, let’s not get carried away, and they kind of did what you would expect them to do.” MORE: Stephen A. Smith blasts Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer after Week 7 press conference The Eagles entered the matchup without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts. Backup Tanner McKee took over, while Philadelphia also lost running back Saquon Barkley to a hamstring injury during the game. Aikman acknowledged that Dallas deserved credit for the victory but believes more evidence is needed before expectations rise. “I did think the Eagles defensively would put up a little bit more of a fight than what they did,” Aikman said. “But, you know, it’ll bear itself out as we move forward as to what this team’s capable of.” Cowboys defense remains the biggest question Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) takes the field at Lincoln Financial Field. item.title: How a month of questions turned Warriors' Yaxel Lendeborg into force that dominated the Nuggets
item.description: Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg hangs from the rim after dunking the ball for a basket in a game against the Nuggets in Denver on Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. (David Zalubowski/Associated Press) DENVER – The questions come in all shapes and all sizes, by text and microphone and the voice of the Warriors ' Yaxel Lendeborg . He wants to know. He does not stop. The questions reflect something growing in Golden State, the beginning of a new generation taking root. How does Stephen Curry stay conditioned? How has Jimmy Butler mastered his rocker-step? How can one earn the respect of the veterans? Lendeborg goes everywhere for the answers, inside the organization and out. After Golden State's blowout win over Denver on Monday night, the rookie even went straight to national television, using a postgame Peacock interview as a chance for him to interview Hall of Famers Carmelo Anthony, Tracy McGrady and Vince Carter. "Do you guys have any advice, like, just for me in general, just to try to keep going and things I gotta work on?" Lendeborg asked with a headset on . "Anything you guys see that I don't see?" He texted a version of the same question to Curry and Draymond Green in early October at the end of Golden State's Hawaii trip, coming away disappointed in himself. Lendeborg entered that game timid. He exited with four points. He didn't want to "mess up" the Curry-Green dynamic, as he said. Their responses? "They pretty much just gave me free roam," Lendeborg said Monday, describing Curry and Green's responses. "So, they helped me out. And from there, I just vowed to be a little more aggressive, each night." This version of Lendeborg Monday night – a bulldozing, unstoppable point forward with the "strength of an ox," as Steve Kerr put it postgame – was an entirely new version from the Lendeborg in Hawaii, and even the Lendeborg in Phoenix on Saturday night . Through four games, he is absorbing at a rate that no rookie has ever shown in Kerr's 13-year career at the helm of the Warriors. It was enough Monday to completely and utterly dominate the second half of a game against the three-time league Most Valuable Player in Nikola Jokic, and win a matchup with vaunted Nuggets veteran Aaron Gordon so thoroughly that Gordon was eventually tossed ( for contesting an illegal screen on Denver teammate Christian Braun ). Gordon didn't dance around any subtlety, asked on Lendeborg postgame. "Yaxel has an opportunity to be special in this league, man," Gordon, a 13-year NBA vet, told the Chronicle. "Just, all the tools, his size, his strength, he has the mentality. He's really good, man. He's ready. It's cool to see Steve Kerr empower him. They got a good one." The shocking reality was that nobody within on a perennial Western Conference contender could stop a 24-year-old rookie playing his fourth NBA game. He head-hunted Jokic at the rim. "His best decision would be to remain with the Yankees as they know exactly how to help him be the best version of himself." item.title: Kingston Flemings Must Become An Aggressive Scorer For Atlanta Hawks
item.description: There is no doubt the Atlanta Hawks are high on newcomer and top-ten pick Kingston Flemings . Flemings, drafted eighth overall in the 2026 NBA Draft, can elevate the Hawks’ offense with his playmaking prowess. Hawks head coach Quin Snyder has given Flemings plenty of run to prove himself early on. Entering Tuesday’s games, Flemings ranks seventh among rookies in total minutes played. In comparison, fellow Hawks rookie Zuby Ejiofor has seen playing time in mop-up duty (22 minutes in four games). The Atlanta staff clearly trusts Flemings with a big role off the bench, but it’s been a mixed bag through four games. Aggressive Scoring Helps Flemings’ Playmaking By trade, Kingston Flemings is a pass-first guard. But there are numerous times when he passes up open shots. Instead, he defers to a teammate. Flemings is a great passer and possesses elite vision. That aspect of his game has been on full display through his first few games. YEAH Kingston pic.twitter.com/7NMh0LPA1J — Atlanta Hawks (@ATLHawks) October 24, 2026 The problems arise when Flemings passes up open shots, which leads to turnovers. In five preseason games, Flemings only turned the ball over five times. He has 11 turnovers through four regular-season games, more than double his preseason rate. He ranks second behind Caleb Wilson and tied with Yaxel Lendeborg in that category. Notably, Flemings ranks third on the Hawks in potential assists (seven), behind Jalen Johnson and Dyson Daniels . While he’s an aggressive passer, he’s a passive scorer, which can be detrimental to the Hawks’ offense. Efficiency Can Increase Flemings’ Shot Tendency So far, Flemings has a 15.4% usage rate when on the floor. Perhaps a reason for his low shot attempts is a lack of confidence to take them, and so far, his inability to make them. Flemings only has a 35.2% true shooting percentage so far this season. This has translated into hesitancy to shoot, even when he has open looks. This lack of confidence will also lead opposing defenses to leave Flemings more space. The bottom line is he must be a more willing scorer. Even though Flemings prefers to share the ball with his teammates, the offense benefits if he also starts looking for his own shot. The good news is that Flemings is already a great on-ball defender and playmaker. He is more than capable of being an elite player on both ends of the floor. Snyder praised Flemings for his defensive efforts after his first game against the Orlando Magic. “I thought [Kingston Flemings] did some really good things,” Snyder said after the game. “He turned up the pressure defensively. We went on a couple of runs during that time where we forced a bunch of turnovers.” Flemings’ potential is off the charts, but he needs to develop aggressive scoring habits to complement the rest of his game.
